title: Solar Ni appendix

products.stat_basis: measured — RMS of the random terms, 0.07555 dex at n_lines=18

components.name: measurement
components.source: per-feature scatter of the accepted pool (components within 0.5 A merged, RYA-1232)

components.name: transition_data
components.source: not in the Asplund+2021 Sect. 2.1 budget (atomic data not included); a pool line carries no published gf sigma

components.name: stellar.logg
components.source: solar log g is pinned; delta_logg is definitionally zero (RYA-1089)

components.name: stellar.metallicity
components.source: solar [Fe/H] is pinned; delta_feh is definitionally zero (RYA-1089)

components.name: stellar.teff
components.source: sourced DEFINED zero (RYA-1226 convention): the solar Teff allowance is 1 K

evidence.owed_measurement: a Teff perturbation on this pool

components.name: model_atmosphere
components.source: |paired median(A[MARCS.GES] - A[ATLAS9.Castelli])| on this pool: the 1D-LTE route against its deck LTE comparand (same lines, fitter and window, departures withheld), only the atmosphere grid varied (RYA-731)

components.name: telluric
components.source: 3000-3780 A contains no registered telluric band (pipeline.telluric_policy)

components.name: blends
components.source: full atomic + molecular synthesis in-window (RYA-1230 turned molecular opacity on in every band); no catalogued-blend deficit

components.name: nlte
components.source: this leg applies no departures (nlte_delta_dex = 0 on every line)

components.name: pseudo_continuum
components.source: outside the near-UV the continuum is observed; it is placed per line by the standing rule and priced on `continuum`

components.name: hfs_isotopes
components.source: every pool line has hfs_n_components == 1 (canonical_gf)

components.name: molecular_coupling
components.source: atomic product; the selector is not a MOL- indicator set

components.name: holding_instrument
components.source: SynthesisHandler harness residual MEASURED against the known optical answer (RYA-869)

components.source: not in the Asplund+2021 Sect. 2.1 budget (stat, atmosphere, half the 3D effect, NLTE); RYA-1315 runs only those legs

components.name: continuum

components.name: profile_ew

body_html:
Solar nickel: 6.283 ± 0.044

Asplund, Amarsi & Grevesse 2021: 6.20 ± 0.04  ·  this measurement +0.083 dex

Asplund, Amarsi & Grevesse (2021) give no line recipe we can repeat for this element, so this is our best HARPS product: the Reference Grade analysis with the most complete treatment, then the most lines.

  • VIS: 6.283 ± 0.044 · HARPS · VIS · Ni I · reference lines · <3D> LTE (Gerber)

Line grades

Every product is measured on one of four grades of spectral lines and the grades are never mixed in one number.

Scroll horizontally to read all columns · focus the table and use the arrow keys

Line grades
GradeWhat it meansThis element
Reference Gradelines from a published solar line set (Asplund et al. 2021 and similar), measured with the oscillator strengths the authors used77 products -- Ni I · reference lines; SET-NI_AGSS21
Codex Gradelines chosen by the Codex whose oscillator strength carries a published uncertainty (laboratory measurement, NIST accuracy class A-C, or the paper's own stated error), between 5% and 60% deep55 products -- Ni I · Codex-graded lines
Deep Gradethe same oscillator-strength rule on lines deeper than 60% -- stronger lines, more sensitive to damping and the model atmosphere21 products -- Ni I · Deep-graded lines
Theoretical Codexlines whose oscillator strength comes from atomic theory, calculated rather than measured in a laboratory and with no published uncertainty, adopted by name after review. Shown on their own and never used for the headline value90 products -- SET-NI_CLEAR2026; SET-NI_ELGUETA2026; SET-NI_ELGUETA2026-FREECONT

How to read this forest. Each row is one independent product, preserving its band, holding, engine, indicator and line set. Engines and indicator families are never averaged. Each bar is the uncertainty as Asplund et al. 2021 quote it: line-to-line scatter, the 3D-model term and the NLTE term (at least 0.03 dex). For a molecule the NLTE term is replaced by its dependence on the other element, and the 3D term comes from the 3D-to-1D difference Amarsi et al. 2021 publish for the same band. Atomic-data and observational terms are not in the bar, as in Asplund; they stay in the full error budget attached to the row. Grades describe the supplied line-pool provenance, not engine quality; evaluated theoretical CNO oscillator strengths are not relabelled as laboratory evidence. Quarantined, failed and unconstrained fits have no abundance mark. Experimental products remain explicitly not adopted. Literature references provide context, never tuning targets. Yellow rows are Deep Grade: strong lines that saturate, kept but less certain than the other grades.

How this was measured

Every nickel value on this page comes from fitting synthetic spectra to the observed solar spectrum, line by line or band by band, with the nickel abundance as the free parameter. The synthesis includes the atomic lines and the molecular opacity in every window, so blended absorption is modelled rather than attributed to the line being measured. The continuum is placed locally around every line by comparing the observation with the synthesis on its own highest pixels, and ground-based spectra are telluric-corrected across their full range.

Each indicator is measured independently on each solar spectrum and reported separately; nothing is averaged across indicators or instruments. Where a 3D or NLTE correction is published for the lines, it is applied as its own product (1D-LTE, 1D-NLTE and 3D-NLTE are separate rows). Every value carries a full uncertainty budget: fit, line strengths, microturbulence, continuum, fit window, model atmosphere, telluric residual, and the spread between spectra, each measured by refitting with that one input changed. The headline at the top is the Asplund-grade product: a published line set, the most complete treatment, then the most lines.

Solar nickel context

Solar nickel is measured from neutral Ni I lines and compared with ionized Ni II. The optical Ni I products include laboratory oscillator strengths. The infrared Ni I set uses the lines Elgueta et al. 2026 identified as reliable for Sun-like stars and calculated oscillator strengths. The Ni II set uses calculated oscillator strengths from Clear et al. 2026. Both sets are shown as Theoretical Codex. The H-band result is sensitive to continuum placement. The nickel model atom supports non-LTE line formation for Ni I.
